name: WEEE Directive
evidence_rating: thin: one Commission evaluation with a supporting study; collection data reported by Member States
summary: The Commission's 2025 evaluation found that collection of waste electronics rose by about 65% between 2012 and 2021, but that nearly half of all e-waste generated in the EU is still not collected, only three Member States met the 65% collection target in 2022, and the recycling targets do little to recover critical raw materials.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

indicators.target_or_baseline: 65% of EEE placed on the market (or 85% of WEEE generated) from 2019
indicators.evidence: Collection up about 65% (2012-2021); nearly half of WEEE generated not collected; three Member States met the target in 2022.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Evaluation of Directive 2012/19/EU on waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE), Commission staff working document (July 2025)
literature.title: Evaluation of Directive 2012/19/EU on waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE)
literature.method: ex-post evaluation (Member State data, supporting study by Ramboll, Umweltbundesamt and Oeko-Institut, consultation)
literature.headline: Collection up about 65% between 2012 and 2021, but nearly half of WEEE not collected; only three Member States met the 65% target in 2022; recycling targets do not drive recovery of critical raw materials
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found more e-waste is collected than before, but most countries miss the target and valuable materials are still lost.
